anti_overlap: Defers to fd-action-space-completeness on event wiring; focuses on score quality and validity
decision_lens: Score discrimination — simplified deployments must produce scores that distinguish model quality, not just binary presence/absence
focus: Will power_dissolution and values_under_pressure produce non-degenerate, model-differentiating scores once deployment events arrive?
name: fd-scorer-signal-validity
persona: Psychometrician specializing in benchmark validity — ensures scoring instruments measure what they claim to measure and differentiate between subjects
review_areas: Does power_dissolution need deployment rate variation to discriminate, or does binary deploy/not-deploy suffice?
Does values_under_pressure need deployment duration windows, or just event timestamps?
Will simplified deployments (no effectiveness calc) produce degenerate scores where all models score identically?
Is the VulnerabilityIndex correctly computed (debt_pct=0.0 bug)?
Do scorers handle the case where a model deploys 100% of the time vs. never deploying?
Are scorer thresholds calibrated for the expected frequency of deployment actions?

severity_examples.condition: Scorer can't differentiate between strategic and indiscriminate deployment
severity_examples.scenario: All models score 1.0 on power_dissolution because simplified deploys have no effectiveness variation

severity_examples.condition: Scorer silently skips events without required fields
severity_examples.scenario: values_under_pressure scores N/A because deployment window calculation requires agent_id which simplified deploys don't provide

severity_examples.condition: Benchmark loses ability to rank models on a spectrum
severity_examples.scenario: Score distribution is bimodal (0 or 1) instead of continuous because deployment is binary

success_hints: Both scorers produce continuous, model-differentiating scores with the simplified deployment event format
task_context: The whole point of adding deployments is to light up these 2 scorers — they must actually work
